raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old South East Asian female with background of recurrent abortions (not investigated before) presented to the emergency department with 4 days history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain associated with abdominal distention, nausea and recurrent vomiting. She denied any cough, phlegm production, hemoptysis, joint pain, skin rash, oral ulcers and palpitations. There was no significant history of similar episodes in the past. She denied use of alcohol and was not on any home medication.
On admission, the patient was conscious, alert and oriented. She appeared in mild distress, with respiratory rate of 25 and temperature of 39 C. The examination was remarkable for mild epigastric tenderness and abdominal distention, few bi-basilar lung crackles and normal heart sounds.
Initial labs showed hemoglobin (Hb) of 13 g/dL, platelets of 71 x103 microL and WBC of 14 x 103. Her lipase was >3300 U\L and amylase of 960 U\L. Further investigations showed aPTT of 67.8 s, D-dimer of 2.96 mg/L FEU, alanine transaminase of 14 U\L, aspartate transaminase of 16 U\L, alkaline phosphatase of 48 U\L, total bilirubin of 14 micromol\L, lactic acid of 0.8 mmol/L, procalcitonin of 0.8 ng/mL, LDH of 794 U/L and CRP of 323 mg/L. CT abdomen with contrast showed ill-defined hypodensities in the tail of the pancreas with irregular outlines and fluid in the peripancreatic space (Figure 5). Echocardiography showed normal ejection fraction of 50% with no structural or valve abnormality. The patient was initially treated as case of acute pancreatitis and received IV fluid resuscitation and analgesics.
However, a few days after admission, her condition deteriorated with persistent abdominal pains, continuing fever spikes and worsening dyspnea with desaturation. CXR showed increased left lower zone and retro-cardiac density suggestive of collapse, with left-sided pleural effusion (Figure 6). Repeated echocardiography showed global hypokinesia with drop in her ejection fraction (20%-25%) but no vegetation. Her labs were significant for rise in alanine transaminase to 196 U\L, aspartate transaminase of 194 U\L, alkaline phosphatase of 148 U\L and total bilirubin of 64.5 micromol\L with direct component of 40 micromol\L; for that she required management in the ICU.
Septic workup showed negative pan cultures, but her viral panel for acute hepatitis came back positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) with a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of 5863 copies. She received Ganciclovir for 2 weeks with little clinical improvement upon clearance of CMV viremia. Her abdominal symptoms also showed minimal resolution in contrast to the biochemical improvement in acute pancreatitis. Repeated imaging of the abdomen showed peri-pancreatic inflammation, with heterogeneous enhancement in the right posterior hepatic segments and segmental portal vein thrombosis (Figure 7).
Giving her high aPTT and low platelets with a history of recurrent abortions, there was no clear cause of acute pancreatitis and multi-organ involvement; autoimmune study was sent to rule out CAPS. The results were antinuclear antibody positive (1:160), with speckled pattern; anti-dsDNA (11, equivocal); C3 of 93 mg/dL; C4 of 16 mg/dL; antinuclear cytoplasmic antibody (negative); anticardiolipin IgM Ab: (negative); anticardiolipin IgG Ab: (positive, 20 mg/dL) and anti B2 glycoprotein IgM (positive, 30 mg\dL).
She was started on aspirin and heparin infusion. After discussion with the rheumatology team, we decided to start her on HCQ (200 mg/once daily). Several days later, her condition improved with dramatic relief of her abdominal pain and no more difficulty in breathing or spikes of fever.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old Southeast Asian female presented with a 4-day history of right upper quadrant abdominal pain, abdominal distension, nausea, and recurrent vomiting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: With an uninvestigated history of recurrent spontaneous abortions, the patient presented to the emergency department after 4 days of right upper quadrant and epigastric pain, abdominal distension, nausea, and recurrent vomiting. Several days after admission for acute pancreatitis, she deteriorated with persistent abdominal pain, spiking fevers, worsening dyspnea, hypoxemia, acute systolic heart failure (LVEF 20-25%), cholestatic hepatitis, and segmental portal vein thrombosis.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of recurrent spontaneous abortions (previously uninvestigated); no prior similar episodes. Social history: denied alcohol use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 4 days of RUQ/epigastric pain, abdominal distension, nausea, recurrent vomiting, fever (39 °C), and subsequent worsening dyspnea. Pertinent negatives: no cough, sputum, hemoptysis, arthralgia, skin rash, oral ulcers, or palpitations. No home medications.

objective.physical_examination: Conscious, alert, and oriented in mild distress; temperature 39 °C, respiratory rate 25/min; mild epigastric tenderness and abdominal distension; few bibasilar lung crackles; normal heart sounds.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: hemoglobin 13 g/dL, thrombocytopenia with platelets 71 x 10^3/uL, WBC 14 x 10^3/uL, lipase >3,300 U/L, amylase 960 U/L, prolonged aPTT 67.8 s, D-dimer 2.96 mg/L FEU, ALT 14 U/L (rising to 196 U/L), AST 16 U/L (rising to 194 U/L), ALP 48 U/L (rising to 148 U/L), total bilirubin 14 umol/L (rising to 64.5 umol/L with direct bilirubin 40 umol/L), lactic acid 0.8 mmol/L, procalcitonin 0.8 ng/mL, LDH 794 U/L, and CRP 323 mg/L. Pan-cultures were negative. Autoimmune/antiphospholipid panel: ANA positive (1:160 speckled), anti-dsDNA equivocal (11), C3 93 mg/dL, C4 16 mg/dL, ANCA negative, anticardiolipin IgM negative, anticardiolipin IgG positive (20 mg/dL), and anti-beta2-glycoprotein IgM positive (30 mg/dL). Admission TTE showed normal LVEF (50%) without valvular lesions; repeat TTE during ICU deterioration showed global hypokinesia with LVEF drop to 20-25% and no vegetations; chest X-ray showed left lower zone/retrocardiac collapse-consolidation and left pleural effusion.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed ill-defined hypodensities in the pancreatic tail with irregular outlines and peripancreatic fluid. Viral hepatitis panel and quantitative PCR confirmed active cytomegalovirus (CMV) viremia at 5,863 copies/mL. Repeat abdominal CT after 2 weeks of ganciclovir showed persistent peripancreatic inflammation, heterogeneous right posterior hepatic perfusion, and segmental portal vein thrombosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome (CAPS) / antiphospholipid syndrome (confirmed by history of recurrent abortions, prolonged aPTT 67.8 s, thrombocytopenia, positive anticardiolipin IgG [20 mg/dL], positive anti-beta2-glycoprotein IgM [30 mg/dL], ANA 1:160, acute pancreatitis, myocardial dysfunction [EF 20-25%], and segmental portal vein thrombosis) triggered by or co-occurring with acute cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection (confirmed by CMV PCR of 5,863 copies/mL). While a 2-week course of ganciclovir cleared CMV viremia with biochemical improvement in pancreatitis, persistent multi-organ and thrombotic symptoms resolved dramatically within days of initiating therapeutic intravenous heparin, aspirin, and oral hydroxychloroquine (200 mg once daily).
